subject.title: fix(line): cap message action text length

question: Should over-limit LINE message-action text be centrally truncated and sent as a different user message, or should OpenClaw use a lossless failure, fallback, or mapped-command policy?
rationale: The helper is shared by quick replies, templates, cards, and rich menus, while LINE defines the field as text sent from the user; source correctness cannot determine whether changing that value is acceptable product behavior.

options.title: Adopt lossless overflow handling
options.body: Have the action-producing path choose an explicit fallback or stable mapped command identifier when text exceeds LINE’s limit, so a tap never sends an unintended prefix.

options.title: Approve central grapheme truncation
options.body: Accept the PR’s behavior as the LINE channel policy and document that over-limit action text intentionally sends its first 300 grapheme clusters.

options.title: Reject over-limit action construction
options.body: Make over-limit message actions fail visibly and require callers to shorten or redesign the interaction before sending.

recommendation.title: Adopt lossless overflow handling
recommendation.body: Have the action-producing path choose an explicit fallback or stable mapped command identifier when text exceeds LINE’s limit, so a tap never sends an unintended prefix.

likelyOwner.reason: No current-main feature-history owner was available without guessing; route through the LINE channel ownership path for an explicit policy decision.
